newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan wants markets to further digest G7 pact--MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan wants markets to further digest G7 pact--MOF.

text.p: Japan hopes an agreement on currencies reached by the Group of Seven (G7) nations at their meeting in late April will be further digested by financial markets, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Friday.

"The content (of the G7 agreement) has gradually filtered through to the markets. However, we are not satisfied with that and hope the impact of the G7 agreement will be further digested by the markets. I will not comment on the issue of currency intervention," Mitsuzuka said.
He also said that the yen has been strengthening in the past few days.
The G7 nations agreed at a meeting in Washington in April that excessive volatility in currency rates and significant deviations from economic fundamentals were undesirable.

They emphasised the importance of avoiding exchange rates that could lead to the reemergence of large external imbalances and agreed to monitor developments and cooperate as appropriate in currency markets.
Asked about intervention in currency markets, Mitsuzuka said: "I won't say whether we will do it or won't do it. We will deal with it as appropriate."
